title: xAI's Grok 4.6 arrives in Microsoft Foundry with a 500K context window
subtitle: The public-preview drop puts xAI's latest frontier model on Azure's governed enterprise stack alongside OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, and Mistral offerings.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: xAI's Grok 4.6 became available in Microsoft Foundry as a public preview on August 27, 2026. The model is exposed through Foundry's unified catalog with a 500,000-token context window, configurable reasoning levels, and support for long-running agents and interactive visual work. Enterprise customers get the same operational controls Foundry applies to OpenAI's GPT-5.6 and Anthropic's Claude family — evaluation harnesses, deployment gating, and data-residency pins.

The distribution deal matters because it is the second Grok generation to land on Foundry after Microsoft's cautious trials of Grok 4 earlier this year, and it dissolves what had been a significant sales barrier for xAI: many regulated buyers cannot procure directly from xAI but can consume any model that carries Microsoft's governance wrapper. Grok 4.6 launched on August 13 with a Cursor coding partnership and 500K context; the Foundry availability is the enterprise on-ramp that was always the second shoe.

The framing xAI and Microsoft are using is agentic: Grok 4.6 is positioned as a model that can plan across long horizons, recover from tool errors, and continue making progress across extended workflows with minimal supervision. That is the same benchmark story every frontier lab is telling right now — Claude 5 was measured against SWE-agent traces, GPT-5.6 against long-horizon coding, and Gemini 3.7 against browser-use. The competitive battleground has clearly moved past single-turn chat.

For learners: when you see a model land on a hyperscaler's model catalog — Foundry, Bedrock, or Vertex — read that as a distribution event first and a capability event second. The technical numbers were disclosed at the original launch. What's new is that the model is now easier to buy inside a large organization, which is often the actual bottleneck to a model being deployed at scale. Track catalog additions as carefully as you track leaderboards.
